tools.name: explain_transaction
tools.description: Explain a Base-mainnet transaction in plain English. Input: a transaction hash. Returns strict JSON: summary (1-3 sentences), action_type (swap, erc20_transfer, nft_mint, bridge_out, approval_for_all, ...), assets_moved[] (token, amount, from, to), counterparties[] (labeled where known: routers, bri

tools.name: buy_pass
tools.description: Buy a 30-day pass for $9 in USDC on Base via x402: up to 10,000 explain_transaction calls with no per-call payment. Returns a bearer pass token; attach it at _meta["btx/pass"] on MCP calls or as the X-BTX-Pass header on POST /explain. No account; the token is the only proof of purchase. Renew by buy

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "buy_pass" references sensitive artifacts (bearer). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

evidence.snippet: Buy a 30-day pass for $9 in USDC on Base via x402: up to 10,000 explain_transaction calls with no per-call payment. Returns a bearer pass token; attach it at _m…

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp?ref=mcp-registry" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: explain_transaction · Private data: explain_transaction, buy_pass · Public sink: explain_transaction, buy_pass.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: explain_transaction · Private data: explain_transaction, buy_pass · Public sink: explain_transaction, buy_pass

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "explain_transaction" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
